findings.title: Session cache invalidation can miss transcript changes with unchanged size and mtime
findings.where: scripts/session-blob-row.mjs:255 builds the signature solely from parser version plus each path's mtimeMs and size; scripts/session-blob-cache-parity.test.mjs:300 explicitly exercises only an edit whose mtime and size both change.
findings.what: A transcript can be replaced with different same-length bytes and have its original mtime restored. Its signature then remains identical, so the sig gate skips parsing and serves stale session_blob-derived datasets and recommendations despite changed source evidence.
findings.fix: Include a content-derived digest in the session signature, computed through the existing capped reader or a streaming capped hash, and extend the parity test with a same-length rewrite followed by restoration of the original file times.
findings.acceptance: After initial ingest, rewrite one fixture transcript with different bytes of exactly the same length, restore its original atime/mtime, and ingest again; assert reparsed is 1, that session's content_hash changes, its assembled data reflects the new bytes, and the untouched session remains byte-identical.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read scripts/session-blob-row.mjs:255-268 and scripts/session-blob-cache-parity.test.mjs:256-334. The signature contains no content component, while the only mutation case deliberately changes both metadata fields, so the collision remains reproducible at the audited baseline.
